title: Treasury Repurchase Agreement Risk Management Recommendation FAQs

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York / Treasury Market Practices Group

summary: The Treasury Market Practices Group (TMPG) released best practice recommendations on U.S. Treasury repo risk management, calling for consistent application of haircuts and margin on repurchase agreements to address systemic risks in the non-centrally cleared bilateral repo market. The TMPG identifies significant inconsistencies and lack of transparency in current bilateral repo risk management practices that could pose threats to financial stability during market stress.
key_points: TMPG recommends all Treasury repos should include haircuts or margin reflecting counterparty credit risk, liquidity risk, and market risk
Bilateral repo market lacks consistency and transparency in risk management practices, making full leverage exposure potentially misunderstood by market participants
Large quantities of unhedged repo positions could pose systemic risks to overall market functioning if participants default
Working group formed February 2023 included dealers, money funds, hedge funds, asset managers, FMUs, clearing banks, foreign central banks, Treasury, and NY Fed staff
Implementation deadline set for June 2026 with rolling, risk-based approach prioritizing material counterparty exposures
Centrally cleared repo already adheres to recommended best practices through existing CCP margining regimes
why_it_matters: The U.S. repo market is foundational to short-term funding and market liquidity. This guidance directly addresses systemic vulnerabilities by pushing all bilateral repo counterparties toward consistent margin practices. Market participants will need to update legal agreements, policies, and collateral management systems before the June 2026 deadline. (Note: $4+ trillion market size figure not verified in source—should be attributed to external data if included.)
market_structure_context: The document provides detailed market structure guidance on repo market risk management. Key elements include: (1) haircuts should reflect counterparty credit risk, liquidity risk, and market risks; (2) legally enforceable documentation required for margining regime including timing, frequency, thresholds, valuation, and close-out provisions; (3) netting agreements and portfolio margining can supplement but not replace haircuts; (4) centrally cleared repos already compliant; (5) repo intermediated into central clearing still requires bilateral risk management between client and facilitating participant.
